clue.text: Container in mind for rifle

indicators.note: in says the container word sits inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't care'
a bin is a container for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a gun stored somewhere in the back of their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbine is a short-barrelled rifle, originally carried by cavalry.

clue.text: No matter when, party in the end consumed by self-loathing?

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside the following word

parts.note: being against oneself, anti-me; the question mark flags the invented word

indicators.note: in the end takes the final letter of party

explanation.surface: A party that ended in self-hatred, whenever it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-loathing?' is read as ANTI-ME, being against me.
explanation.definitionFit: Anytime means at whatever moment, regardless of when.

clue.text: Ridiculously bad cabinet minister ultimately a boring tool

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests absurd disorder, so the letters are mixed up
ultimately takes the final letter of minister

explanation.surface: A dull, useless cabinet minister dismissed as a boring tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculously' rearranges BADCABINET plus R. 'Boring' looks like 'dull', but it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace and bit is a hand drill, a cranked handle turning a boring bit.

clue.text: Hypothetical solution to sum never extremely diabolical

indicators.note: diabolical means dreadfully bad, so the letters are in a mess
extremely takes the outer letters of never

explanation.surface: A dreadful sum that will never be solved, except in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diabolical' rearranges TOSUM with N and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet remedy or scheme whose effectiveness is unproven, a supposed cure.

clue.text: Put in angle — in briefly?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: fashionable only for a short while

indicators.note: in places the word for put inside the word for angle

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
to put something in is to add it

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction to insert something at an angle, ending in a puzzled question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in briefly' is the definition: something faddish is 'in' (in fashion), but only for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddish thing is a passing craze, popular or 'in' for only a brief spell.

clue.text: See 3
I slid coat off, relaxed after being pumped up?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone at the gym shrugging off their coat to unwind after pumping iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ISLIDCOAT. 'Pumped up' suggests a bodybuilder; here it is the heart pumping blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastolic describes the heart's relaxation phase, which follows each contraction that pumps blood.

clue.text: Tories all repent, not half floundering — look away, if you don't want to know!

definitions.text: look away, if you don't want to know!

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are jumbled
not half keeps only the first half of repent

explanation.surface: Conservatives half-heartedly saying sorry while flailing, and a warning to avert one's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler alert warns readers that a plot twist follows, so they can avoid reading.

clue.text: Player catching a target with smooth stone

parts.note: to sand is to smooth with sandpaper

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the stone word contains the target

parts.note: a rock is a stone
the bull is the centre of a target, the bullseye

explanation.surface: An athlete hitting a target with a polished stone, as in curling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' looks like a sportsman, matching the surface, but here it means an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra Bullock is an American film actress, and a player is an actor.

clue.text: Star group written about in contemporary literature

indicators.note: written about means set down turned round, read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A constellation featured in modern fiction, fittingly also Philip Pullman's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns ARYL, taken from inside 'contemporary literature', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra, the Lyre, is a small northern constellation containing the bright star Vega.

clue.text: Sudden pain working for plant

parts.note: a snap decision is a sudden one
a drag is a pain, a tiresome thing
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A sudden ache while gardening, perhaps caused by a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, Antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like jaws.

clue.text: Some criminal, in earnest, going straight

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A criminal who is serious about going straight after prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going straight' looks like reforming, but here it simply means running in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in or along a straight line.

clue.text: In a particular way, maybe the Guardian's saved in time

indicators.note: saved means kept inside, so the paper's word holds the other letters

parts.note: the Guardian is an example of a daily newspaper; 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: The newspaper explaining that it was rescued in the nick of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved' here means kept inside, not rescued; 'maybe' marks the Guardian as one example of a newspaper published every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daintily means delicately or fastidiously, a particular and fussy manner of doing things.

clue.text: Leader May frantic — something cooked up in advance

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: Prime Minister Theresa May in a frenzy, with a scheme prepared beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal is a supermarket dish prepared beforehand, needing only reheating.

clue.text: 'Dress in a state', declares expert fashion designer

parts.note: to don clothes is to dress in them
to tell is to state or relate
avers means asserts or declares
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A designer quoted making a dramatic claim about a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatella Versace is the Italian designer who heads the Versace fashion house.

clue.text: See 8
Grapes not available then? Fleeced?

definitions.note: an adjective here: having a fleece, like a sheep

parts.note: nothing available, nil, zero, O
grapes grow on a vine

explanation.surface: A wry question about a wine harvest failing and someone being swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeced' looks like 'cheated', but the definition means woolly, like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, the animals that grow fleeces.

clue.text: See 15
Minute error initially in damaged travel pass

indicators.note: in places the minute and the letter inside the word for damaged

parts.note: bust means broken or damaged
a tick is a moment, a minute

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of error

explanation.surface: A small mistake on a broken travel pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus ticket is the document that lets a passenger travel on a bus.

clue.text: Balls move from side to side after Tottenham taking the lead?

indicators.note: after puts the waddling word behind the Tottenham letter
taking the lead picks the first letter of Tottenham

parts.note: to waddle is to walk swaying from side to side

explanation.surface: Footballers swerving the ball after Tottenham go in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Waddle played for Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club. 'Balls' is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is British slang for nonsense, a synonym of drivel.

clue.text: Creole tune originally played as synthesised music

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement
originally takes the opening letter of tune

explanation.surface: A Creole melody performed on synthesisers.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is a genre of electronic dance music built on synthesisers and drum machines.

clue.text: Awfully clean on top of table, surgeon's knife

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are scrambled
on top of takes the first letter of table

explanation.surface: A surgeon's knife lying on an operating table that is not properly clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a small double-edged surgical blade used for incisions.

clue.text: Embarrassing blunder by blackguard, fellow punching bore

indicators.note: punching means breaking into, so the pair goes inside the word for bore

parts.note: to pall is to become tiresome, to bore
a rat is a scoundrel or blackguard

explanation.surface: A scoundrel and his friend punching a tedious man, an embarrassing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A pratfall is a fall on one's backside, figuratively a humiliating mistake.

clue.text: Tory with top story thus appearing in many papers

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: appearing in puts the story and thus inside the word for many papers

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets
the lead is a newspaper's main story
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician whose big story is splashed across many newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top story' is newspaper jargon for the main front-page item. Andrea Leadsom was a British Conservative cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Leadsom is a Conservative MP who stood for party leader in 2016.

clue.text: Were a couple old-fashioned?

definitions.meaning: went out together romantically, past tense
out of date, no longer in style

explanation.surface: Asking whether a couple's relationship was traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated is the past tense of going out romantically, and also an adjective meaning outmoded.

clue.text: Article secured by French detectives — for a tanner?

definitions.note: a substance used by someone who tans leather

indicators.note: secured by means held between, so the article sits in the middle

parts.note: Gallic means French, from Gaul
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: French detectives securing an item, perhaps for a sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is an old British sixpence coin, but here it is a leather worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic acid, found in oak galls, is a substance used in tanning leather.

clue.text: Ferry terminal in Felixstowe has shot ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the drink in front of the end letter

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a shot

indicators.note: terminal in takes the last letter of Felixstowe

explanation.surface: Felixstowe port, a ferry terminal, where someone drinks before sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferry' looks like a boat, but it is a verb meaning to carry. Felixstowe is an English port in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, and to ferry is to carry or transport.

clue.text: Sentence perhaps key, last of many by writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of many

explanation.surface: Choosing a key for a sentence by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' looks grammatical; here it is a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment, and a prison sentence is one example.

clue.text: See 24
